voiceSummary: Oil India Limited announced the outcome of its Board Meeting held on 12th November 2026. The Board approved the Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and half-year ended 30th September 2026 on both Standalone and Consolidated bases, along with the Limited Review Report by Auditors. attchmntText: Oil India Limited has informed the Exchange regarding a press release dated November 12, 2026, titled "OIL reported 20% growth in crude oil production resulting to 116% growth in Standalone PAT during Q2 FY27".
voiceSummary: Oil India Limited reported financial results for Q2 FY27 following its Board meeting on 12th November 2026. The company recorded a 20% growth in crude oil production and a 116% increase in Standalone Profit After Tax to Rs. 2,259 crore. Consolidated PAT rose 53% to Rs. 2,521 crore. The Board recommended an interim dividend of Rs. 7.00 per equity share. Crude oil price realization increased by 35% to USD 92.24 per barrel. Subsidiary NRL achieved a 265% growth in Gross Refining Margin to US$ 28.24 per barrel. The refinery maintained capacity utilization of over 100%. The company drilled 42 wells in the first half of the year.

attchmntText: Oil India Limited has submitted to the Exchange, the financial results for the period Quarter and Half-year ended September 30, 2026.
voiceSummary: Oil India Limited Board of Directors meeting held on 12th November 2026 approved Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended 30th September 2026. The Board declared an Interim Dividend of Rs. 71 per share, representing 70 percent of paid-up capital for the financial year 2026-27. The dividend shall be paid on or before 12th December 2026. The Record Date for ascertaining shareholder eligibility is set as Friday, 20th November 2026. The financial results include a Limited Review Report from auditors RKP Associates and OPTotla & Co. The auditors noted an Emphasis of Matter regarding provisions for Service Tax and GST liability on royalty, totaling Rs. 5,283.85 crore as at 30th September 2026. Additionally, the report highlights a contingent liability of Rs. 2,484.81 crore raised by the Government of Assam. The auditors also noted non-compliance with the Companies Act 2013 regarding the number of Independent Directors and the absence of a Woman Director during the period.
